gen-fs-nippo-montserrat: Montserrat glides under the eye, its curves entered through generous white space, while Nippo's wiry strokes cut sharp above it. Shrink the heading and its proud small letters lose that bite.
gen-fs-nippo-rubik: Rubik reads soft and clear, its big lowercase and open round letters holding up at small sizes. And Nippo's cut-wire strokes give the heading a technical edge, with small letters standing nearly capital-sized.
gen-fs-nunito-fs-karma: Soft and cozy up top: Nunito's curves refuse to close, and Karma's serif terminals finish well clear of the stem below. Karma's gentle modulation never snags the eye on its way.
gen-fs-oswald-bitter: Oswald packs its rows of text tightly, confident and strong. What stands out most is grounded footing: Bitter, a slab-serif with a very large lowercase eye and a see-through gap in each s.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-chillax: Oswald sets tight, confident rows of text in a display voice. Chillax loosens things up with a smooth, tube-like line and casual pen-lifted curves that leave their loops unfinished.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-epilogue: Oswald brings tightly knit, confident rows of display text. Epilogue, a plain sans with a tall-bodied lowercase and wire-like monoline strokes, supplies the pair's most striking quality: curvy, unclamped looseness.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-erode: Tightly knit rows give Oswald its confident, strong look. Erode, a text serif, keeps a tall middle band and shallow ascenders, and its weight ebbs and flows so reading glides on.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-gambetta: Oswald does strength best, packing tightly knit rows with confidence. Gambetta, a text serif, does bookish grace, with wide channels into each counter and soft accents of heavier strokes.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-hind: Tightly knit rows of confident display type make Oswald hard to miss. Hind, a sans with lowercase nearly matching the capitals and strokes steady as a drawn string, keeps reading smooth and unhurried.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-hoover: Tight, confident, strong: Oswald stacks its rows close and means it. Hoover, a serif with a generous entry into the e's eye and compressed ascenders, makes reading feel refined and sturdy.
